structure.text:
Received: 15 November 2005 / Revised: 3 March 2006 / Accepted: 7 March 2006 / Published online: 29 April 2006 © Springer-Verlag 2006

**Abstract** Al, F-doped new perovskite lithium ion conductors  $\text{Li}_{3x}\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\alpha}1/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$  (x=0.11) have been prepared by solid state reaction. It is found that a pure perovskite-structured phase with space group of P4mm(99) exits in the composition range of  $0 < y \le 0.10$ . The sample with y=0.02 possesses the highest ionic conductivity of  $1.06 \times 10^{-3}$  S/cm at room temperature, and its decomposing voltage is 2.3 V. The factors affecting the conductivity of this system are discussed.

**Keywords** Perovskite · Lithium fast ion conductor · LLT · Ionic conductivity · Al, F-doped

structure.title: Introduction
structure.text:
Lithium fast ion conductors are of great interest for their potential use as electrolyte of full solid-state batteries and in other electrochemical devices. Of these materials,  $\text{Li}_{3x}\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\Box}1/3-2x}\text{TiO}_3$  (LLT), where  $\Box$  represents vacancy with a perovskite-related structure, has attracted peculiar attention for its high lithium ion conductivity of  $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$  S/cm at room temperature when  $x\approx0.10$  [1]. To further improve lithium ion conductivity, much effort has been dedicated to substitute A-site La by other cations, such as other rare earth cations or alkaline earth cations, and/or substitute B-site Ti by other trivalent, tetravalent, pentavalent or hexavalent cations [2–13]. So far, only doping Sr up to 5% [12] and partial substitution of Al for Ti [10] are reported to increase the ionic conductivity slightly.

Based on these research, the ionic conductivity is proposed to depend mainly on the following factors [1, 10-13]:

- The size of the A-site cation. As lithium ion conductivity originates from the motion of lithium along the A-site vacancies, the window of four oxygens separating adjacent A sites constitute the bottleneck for lithium ion migration. Thus, La substituted by smaller ions reduces the bottleneck size and suppresses the lithium ion migration, while the substitution of larger ions increases the bottleneck size and enhances the ion migration.
- Lithium ion and vacancy concentration in the A sublattice.
- 3. Ordering or disordering of La, Li, and vacancies. The more the arrangement of their distribution is ordered, the lower the conductivity will be.
- 4. The facility of tilting of TiO<sub>6</sub> octahedra. The easier the tilting the higher the ionic conductivity.
- 5. The local structure. The local lattice distortion will increase the activation energy of ionic conductivity and will decrease the ionic conductivity.
- 6. The change of bond strength between A–O and B–O bond in ABO<sub>3</sub> perovskites. Stronger B–O bond favors high ionic conductivity.

In this study, a new perovskite solid solution with F and Al co-doped LLT were synthesized for the first time and characterized by AC impedance spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and DC polarization.

Electrical conductivity was measured by an AC impedance technique on reheated discs (13-mm diameter and about 2-mm thick) from room temperature to 400 °C in the frequency range of 0.1 Hz-8 MHz. The entire cell assembly was placed in a tubular furnace, in which the temperature could be controlled to  $\pm 2$  °C with a temperature controller (model YCC-1211) for impedance measurement. Decomposing voltage of the sample was measured by DC polarization experiment using graphite as both of the electrodes in the voltage range of 0– 4.0 V in air. All the measurements of electrochemical properties were carried out in ZAHNER Elektrik Thales IM6 Station (Germany).

structure.text:
X-ray diffraction analysis

Figure 1 shows the powder XRD patterns of the  $\text{Li}_{3x}$   $\text{La}_{2/3-x^{-1}/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$  (x=0.11) system. No impurity phase is found to exit along with the perovskite phase in the studied composition range of y<0.10 except for y=0, with  $\text{TiO}_2$  exiting as a second phase. Cubic superstructure reflection lines, stemming from the ordering of  $\text{La}^{3+}$ ,  $\text{Li}^{+}$ , and vacancies or alternate arrangement of  $\text{La}^{-1}$ 

![](_page_1_Figure_7.jpeg)

**Fig. 1** XRD patterns of  $\text{Li}_{3x}\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\Box}1/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$  (x=0.11)

rich and La-poor layers along C-axis, which nearly doubles c-axis [1, 10–12], are observed in all the studied samples and denoted as asterisks in Fig. 1. From the XRD data, we can find that the strength of the superstructure reflections fluctuate slightly with increasing y value and that not all the superstructure reflection lines change in the same trend. This means that the ordering arrangement of La<sup>3+</sup>, Li<sup>+</sup>, and vacancies along the c-axis depends on the composition slightly.

With the use of X'Pert Plus to refine the structure of the samples, all the reflection lines can be indexed in tetragonal structure with space group of P4mm (99), as shown in Fig. 1. The calculation results of unit-cell parameters are listed in Table 1.

It is found that the volume of unit-cell decreases with increasing value of y from y=0.01 to y=0.05, then begins to increase until y=0.07. After that, it resumes to decrease to a minimum value. It is very easy to understand that the volume decreases with an increase of y, as the radius of  $F^-$  (r=136 pm) and  $Al^{3+}$  (r=50 pm) is smaller than that of  $O^{2-}$  (r=140 pm) and  $Ti^{4+}$  (r=68 pm), respectively. With a further increase of the y value, excessive substitution will distort the structure, leading to cell distension in a certain substitution range.

To clarify the effect of F substitution, F-doped solid solution $\text{Li}_{3x-0.02}\text{La}_{0.67-x}\text{TiO}_{2.98}\text{F}_{0.02}$ was synthesized by the same method. The results of conductivity measurements show that the bulk ionic conductivity at RT is in the order of $10^{-4}$ S/cm, with the highest one of $3.17\times10^{-4}$ S/cm for x=0.11. Thus, the current is kept constant at 3.0–3.3 V and resumes to increase until LiOH begins to decompose. Upon scanning the voltage from 5.00 to 0 V, the ionic current keeps decreasing until only the electronic current remains. It is found from Table 2 that the ionic conductivity fluctuates with y value, i.e., the ionic conductivity increases when y increases from 0 to 0.02, then it decreases with a further increase of the y value to 0.06. When y=0.07, the ionic conductivity reaches another peak value, after which the conductivity resumes to decrease with an increase of the y value. Since the concentration of vacancy and lithium ion does not change with the value of y in the present ![](_page_3_Figure_6.jpeg) Fig. 5 Cyclic voltammetry profile for sample of 2LTF measured in air with sample sandwiched between two graphite electrodes system $\text{Li}_{3x}\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\Box}1/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$ (x=0.11), the ratio of vacancy to lithium ion, which may play a role in affecting conductivity, can be ruled out. The ordering of cations and vacancies at A site should not play a major role, as cubic superstructure reflections exit in all the samples and their strengths change slightly with the y value. To explain the changing trend of ionic conductivity, the following factors should be considered: - Size of bottleneck. If the value of y does not increase to such a degree that can distort the tetragonal structure, more Ti4+ and O2- will be replaced by smaller sized Al3+ and F- respectively, when the y value increases. This leads to the contraction of the unit-cell as we discussed previously, allowing the reduction of bottleneck size for Li+ migration and making it more difficult for TiO6 octahedra to tilt [10, 12]. Hence, the ionic conductivity will decrease, but with more Al and F being introduced to the system, the tetragonal structure will be distorted, which makes the volume of unit-cell begin to increase, and a peak value appears at y=0.07. Hence, the bottleneck size is enlarged; accordingly, the conductivity reaches another peak value at y=0.07. - The change of bond strength between A-O and B-O bond in ABO3 perovskites. It has been suggested that the bond strengths of A-O and B-O in ABO3 perovskite are competing because they use the same 2p oxygen orbitals [10, 12]. That is, the stronger the A–O bond, the weaker the B–O bond and vice versa, and the strength of an ionic bond is dominated by the interionic distance and the covalent character of the bond [10, 12]. The shorter the interionic distance, the stronger the ionic bond [10, 12]. When smaller Al3+ replaces Ti4+, the B-O bond will be shortened. Hence, the B-O bond will be strengthened, weakening the Li-O bond, and the mobility of Li+ will be enhanced. On the other hand, the polarizing ability of Al3+ is slightly weaker than that of Ti4+ and Al doping will enhance the ionic character of B-O bond, i.e., enhance the B-O bond and weaken the Li-O bond. As a consequence, the conductivity increases from y=0 to y=0.02. - 3. F is the most electronegative element. The bond between F and other metal elements is mainly of ionic character since the charge of F- is only half of O2-. The electrostatic force between cations and F- will be nearly half of that between cations and O2- since the charge of B-site cations is much higher than that of Li+. The degree of absolute weakening of B-F bond compared to B-O bond is much larger than that of Li-F bond compared to Li-O bond. Thus, F substitution will enhance the competitiveness of Li-F bond, i.e., strengthen the Li-F bond relatively. Thus, the mobility of Li+ will be weakened and the ionic conductivity will decrease as a result. Mainly because of the co-impact of the aforementioned factors, the ionic conductivity shows the fluctuating trend along the *y* value.

nodes.title: Electrochemical Stability via Cyclic Voltammetry
nodes.text:
To see what will happen when the voltage scans back to 0 V, cyclic voltammetry measurement for sample of 2 LTF between 0–5.0 V was taken. The profile is shown in Fig. 5. When the voltage is lower than 2.0 V, the current is low and exhibits a linear relationship with voltage. Such a low current is mainly contributed by the electronic current and small part of the ionic current. Once the voltage is higher than 2.0 V, the current deviates from the linear relationship, then increases sharply when the voltage is higher than 2.3 V, indicating that the sample started to decompose and lithium ion was reduced to lithium on the interface of the cathode and the sample. nodes.title: Mechanisms Explaining Ionic Conductivity Variation
nodes.text:
It is found from Table 2 that the ionic conductivity fluctuates with y value, i.e., the ionic conductivity increases when y increases from 0 to 0.02, then it decreases with a further increase of the y value to 0.06. When y=0.07, the ionic conductivity reaches another peak value, after which the conductivity resumes to decrease with an increase of the y value. Since the concentration of vacancy and lithium ion does not change with the value of y in the present __IMG_46721e2c__ Fig. 5 Cyclic voltammetry profile for sample of 2LTF measured in air with sample sandwiched between two graphite electrodes

system  $\text{Li}_{3x}\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\Box}1/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$  (x=0.11), the ratio of vacancy to lithium ion, which may play a role in affecting conductivity, can be ruled out. The ordering of cations and vacancies at A site should not play a major role, as cubic superstructure reflections exit in all the samples and their strengths change slightly with the y value. To explain the changing trend of ionic conductivity, the following factors should be considered:

- Size of bottleneck. If the value of y does not increase to such a degree that can distort the tetragonal structure, more Ti<sup>4+</sup> and O<sup>2-</sup> will be replaced by smaller sized Al<sup>3+</sup> and F<sup>-</sup> respectively, when the y value increases. This leads to the contraction of the unit-cell as we discussed previously, allowing the reduction of bottleneck size for Li<sup>+</sup> migration and making it more difficult for TiO<sub>6</sub> octahedra to tilt [10, 12]. Hence, the ionic conductivity will decrease, but with more Al and F being introduced to the system, the tetragonal structure will be distorted, which makes the volume of unit-cell begin to increase, and a peak value appears at y=0.07. Hence, the bottleneck size is enlarged; accordingly, the conductivity reaches another peak value at y=0.07. - The change of bond strength between A-O and B-O bond in ABO<sub>3</sub> perovskites. It has been suggested that the bond strengths of A-O and B-O in ABO<sub>3</sub> perovskite are competing because they use the same 2p oxygen orbitals [10, 12]. That is, the stronger the A–O bond, the weaker the B–O bond and vice versa, and the strength of an ionic bond is dominated by the interionic distance and the covalent character of the bond [10, 12]. The shorter the interionic distance, the stronger the ionic bond [10, 12]. When smaller Al<sup>3+</sup> replaces Ti<sup>4+</sup>, the B-O bond will be shortened. Hence, the B-O bond will be strengthened, weakening the Li-O bond, and the mobility of Li<sup>+</sup> will be enhanced. On the other hand, the polarizing ability of Al<sup>3+</sup> is slightly weaker than that of Ti<sup>4+</sup> and Al doping will enhance the ionic character of B-O bond, i.e., enhance the B-O bond and weaken the Li-O bond. As a consequence, the conductivity increases from y=0 to y=0.02.
- 3. F is the most electronegative element. The bond between F and other metal elements is mainly of ionic character since the charge of F<sup>-</sup> is only half of O<sup>2-</sup>. The electrostatic force between cations and F<sup>-</sup> will be nearly half of that between cations and O<sup>2-</sup> since the charge of B-site cations is much higher than that of Li<sup>+</sup>. The degree of absolute weakening of B-F bond compared to B-O bond is much larger than that of Li-F bond compared to Li-O bond. Thus, F substitution will enhance the competitiveness of Li-F bond, i.e., strengthen the Li-F bond relatively. Thus, the mobility of Li<sup>+</sup> will be weakened and the ionic conductivity will decrease as a result. Mainly because of the co-impact of the aforementioned factors, the ionic conductivity shows the fluctuating trend along the *y* value.

structure.title: **Conclusion**
structure.text:
Al,F-doped perovskite lithium ion conductors  $\text{Li}_{3x}$   $\text{La}_{2/3-x^{\text{o}}1/3-2x}\text{Ti}_{1-y}\text{Al}_y\text{O}_{3-y}\text{F}_y$  (x=0.11) have been synthesized. Al substitution enhances the ionic conductivity, while F substitution improves the electrochemical stability. The sample with the initial composition of y=0.02 possesses the best conductivity of  $1.06\times10^{-3}$  S/cm at RT, and its decomposing voltage is 2.3 V. Though from thermodynamic point of view, LLT-based lithium ion conductors cannot be used as electrolyte for batteries using Li as anode [16]. It could be used as electrolyte in lithium ion batteries with open circuit voltage lower then 2.3 V.

It could be used as electrolyte in lithium ion batteries with open circuit voltage lower then 2.3 V.
